title: Impact of biophilic design parameters on university Students' place attachment and quality of campus life
research_question: What is the impact of perceived physical, visual, and auditory nature connectedness (biophilic design parameters) on university students' quality of campus life (self-reported physical health, mental well-being, social health, and academic success) and place attachment (place identity and place dependence)?

participants.description: University students in Tabriz, Iran. Majority female (58.5%), native (72%), single (55.6%). Mean age 24.59 years (SD:8.38). Majority undergraduates (56.1%).
participants.recruitment: Simple random sampling method was used to select participants. Participants were briefed on research objectives and how to answer questions. Only willing participants were included.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: The study investigated students' perceptions of biophilic design parameters (physical, visual, and auditory connections with nature) present on the campus of Islamic Azad University of Tabriz, Iran. This included elements like water features, green space, green walls, natural materials, natural scenes/images, and nature-related sounds (water, wind, birdsong).

mechanisms: Biophilic design elements foster stronger emotional connections to the campus, enhance physical and social well-being, and ultimately improve the overall QCL for students.
Exposure to natural settings has a positive impact on the bonding between people and places, leading to increased PA.
Higher levels of physical nature experience also increase place dependence.
Viewing natural elements and visuals improves overall well-being and satisfaction, increasing PA.
Nature-related sounds such as birdsong and water sounds have a positive but weak relationship with social gatherings.
Direct interaction with nature is linked to better physical health, increased physical activity, weight control, and reduced fatigue among students.
Green spaces in university campuses have also been found to increase physical well-being while window views towards green spaces in classrooms improve the quality of life.
Biophilic designs' elements, such as hearing nature-based sounds, can positively impact students' mood and mental well-being.
Green space connectivity can prompt students' social interactions, and colourful plants promote positive association with students' social activities.
Interaction with water features and green spaces can have a positive impact on academic success.
implementation_implications: Urban planners and designers can use these insights to create more student-centric, nature-integrated urban spaces, promoting the well-being and academic success of university students in densely populated urban areas.

Architects and landscape designers can benefit from this research by incorporating biophilic elements, such as green spaces, natural lighting, and sustainable materials, into their designs to create more engaging and pleasant campus environments.

University administrators can use these insights to prioritise the integration of biophilic elements in their campuses, fostering a stronger sense of place attachment and improved campus life quality for students.

These results can inform public policymakers interested in promoting healthier and more sustainable urban university environments, contributing to the overall well-being of students and enhancing the overall educational experience.

limitations: Students' QCL factors, such as physical health, mental well-being, social health, and academic success, were measured subjectively and through self-reporting, which may limit the generalisability of study findings.
Self-reporting primarily captures conscious, articulated experiences, and preferences. It may not adequately capture non-conscious or subtle responses to biophilic design elements.
Participants may not always be aware of the full extent of their sensory experiences or the influence of these elements on their well-being.
The limited research on the significance of nature-related sounds can result in an incomplete understanding of the role of auditory elements in biophilic design.
It is challenging to draw concrete conclusions about how these sounds may affect students' place attachment and campus life quality.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Humans possess an innate tendency to connect with nature and other living systems, leading to positive psychological and physiological outcomes.
Individuals develop emotional bonds with specific places, and these bonds are influenced by environmental characteristics and contribute to well-being.

mechanism_chain.description: Perceived biophilic design parameters enhance students' place attachment, which in turn partially mediates the relationship with and improves their quality of campus life.
